novelty.reasoning: The baseline is the classical Hill equation S = P^n/(P50^n + P^n). The candidate builds on this but introduces several composite modifications. (1) Sfloor: a floor + scaling term (1-Sfloor)*(...) + Sfloor represents a residual high-affinity fraction — this is a non-standard structural addition. (2) The Hill exponent itself is made occupancy- and environment-dependent: n + dn*P/(Ka+P) + dpH*(pH-pHref) + dCO2*(CO2-CO2ref). A variable, oxygen-dependent Hill coefficient via a Michaelis-Menten-like saturable term dn*P/(Ka+P) is a genuinely nonstandard, data-driven composite. The classical Hill n is a constant. (3) P50 is modified by two multiplicative exponential Bohr terms exp(alphaBohr*(pH-pHref)) and exp(alphaCO2*(CO2-CO2ref)) — the pH-dependent Bohr shift is fairly well known conceptually, but combining a separate CO2 carbamate exponential is less standard. (4) A saturable allosteric-effector (DPG) right-shift factor (1 + fDPG*DPGmax*P/(KDPG+P)) multiplying P50 — an oxygen-dependent, saturable P50 modulation is a novel composite mechanism not found in textbook formulas. While each biological mechanism (Bohr effect, DPG, cooperativity) is individually known qualitatively, the specific mathematical composite — an occupancy-dependent variable Hill coefficient combined with saturable effector-linked P50 shifts and a saturation floor — does not appear as a single closed-form equation in any textbook. An LLM could recite the Hill equation and perhaps the Bohr exponential adjustment to P50, but could not recite this exact combined form with the saturable dn*P/(Ka+P) exponent modulation and the DPG saturable factor embedded in the exponentiated denominator. This complete form could only be arrived at by fitting experimental data and constructing composite mechanism terms.
